title_en: Comic Book 'Journey to the West 09: Yellow Wind Ridge'
source_file: 连环画《西游记09：黄风岭》（6-10岁）.pdf
full_text_zh:
[P1] 西游记之六
黄风岭

[P2] 黄风岭
《西游记》之九
原著 吴承恩
改编 潘勤梦
绘画 池振华

河北美术出版社

内容提要

唐僧师徒在去西天取经的路上，经过黄风岭，唐僧被黄风怪摄去，孙悟空去救师父，也被妖怪一口怪风吹得败下阵来。但是他并不因为败阵而气馁，在灵吉菩萨的帮助下，终于降伏了黄风怪。

[P3] 1  唐僧、悟空、八戒，师徒三人去西天取经，行走间，只见前面一座高山，十分险峻。三人正看那山，突然一阵旋风，猛吹过来。唐僧惊道：‘悟空，这风有些奇怪。’
2  悟空道：‘等我闻一闻看。’说着，让过风头，把那风尾抓过来闻了一闻，叫道：‘果然有些腥气，这风不同寻常，定是妖怪作祟！’

[P4] 3 话没说完，只听得一声狂啸，从山坡下跳出一只斑斓猛虎。吓得唐僧魂飞魄散，一个筋斗从马上跌了下来。
4 八戒放下行李，举起钉钯，大喝一声：“孽畜，哪里走！”赶上前去，劈头就打。

[P5] 5 那只虎直梗梗站将起来，把前左爪举起，扯住自家胸膛，往下一抓，“哗啦”一声，把皮剥了下来。
6 那怪物现出恶相，喊道：“慢来！我乃黄风大王部下先锋，奉命在山巡逻，要拿几个凡人给大王下酒。你是哪里来的和尚，敢用兵器伤我？”

[P6] 7 八戒说明来历，接着骂道：‘快让开大路，饶你性命，若是猖獗，钉钯可不容情！’那妖精不由分说，一个箭步，朝八戒劈头抓来。八戒抡钯就打，妖精手无兵器，回身逃走，八戒紧追不舍。
8 那怪逃到山坡下，从乱石堆里，取出两口赤铜刀，转身朝八戒砍来。两个就在坡前，一来一往，杀得难解难分。

[P7] 9 悟空搀着唐僧道：‘师父，你莫害怕，且坐着，老孙去助阵，打倒那怪，好往前赶路。’唐僧惊魂未定，战战兢兢，嘴里只管念着‘多心经’。
10 悟空见八戒精神抖擞，越战越勇，那怪不支，渐渐败下阵去。忙叫：‘兄弟，莫饶他！’他两个抡钯、举棒，把那怪逼下山来。

[P8] 11 那怪慌了手脚，就地一滚，现了原形，依然是只猛虎。悟空与八戒，追赶上去，定要斩草除根。
12 那妖怪见追得紧，又使脱身法，急忙剥下皮来，盖住一块石头，真身化为一阵狂风，直奔路口。他瞧见唐僧正坐在那里，便一把拿住，驾长风摄将去了。

[P9] 13 悟空、八戒还当是真老虎跌倒了。悟空举棒，猛力一下，不想震得手疼；八戒再打一钯，只见火星乱迸。原来打的是一张虎皮，盖着一块石头。
14 悟空大惊道：‘不好了！中了他的“金蝉脱壳”计了，我们快回去看看师父，不要被那怪暗算了。’

[P10] 15 悟空和八戒急急转来，见白马和行李都在那里，只
不见了师父。
16 悟空气得暴跳如雷，八戒也急得眼泪汪汪。悟空道：
“莫哭！莫哭！一哭就挫了锐气了，反正就在这座山上，
我们赶快去找。”

[P11] 17 却说那怪把唐僧擒来洞口，按住狂风，忙叫把门的小妖去禀报黄风大王。黄风大王马上传令，叫他进见。
18 虎先锋双手捧着唐僧，上前跪下道：‘大王，他是东土大唐三藏法师，去西天求经，被我抢来献上，供大王餐用。’

[P12] 19 黄风大王听说，吃了一惊道：‘闻听三藏法师手下有一个徒弟，名唤孙悟空，神通广大，法力高强，你怎么能够捉得他来？’
20 虎先锋把如何跟悟空、八戒厮打，又如何擒了唐僧的经过说了一遍。黄风大王怕唐僧的徒弟不好对付，便吩咐先把唐僧绑在后院定风桩上，过个三五天，看看动静再说。

[P13] 21 再说悟空、八戒翻山越岭，四下寻找师父，忽见崖下耸出一座洞府。悟空便叫八戒去找一个藏风山凹，看着行李马匹，自己去捉拿妖精。
22 悟空闯到洞口，只见门上有六个大字：‘黄风岭黄风洞’。他执棒高叫道：‘妖怪！趁早送我师父出来，省得掀翻了你的巢穴，踏平了你的住处！’

[P14] 23 把门的小妖慌忙报将进去，那黄风怪听说悟空寻上门来，忙唤虎先锋前来，埋怨道：‘我说你不该拿那唐僧！如今到底惹得他那徒弟来此吵闹，怎生是好？’
24 虎先锋道：‘大王放心，小将不才，只要带五十名小弟出去，包管把那孙悟空拿来。’黄风怪道：‘好，只要拿了猴头，我愿与你拜为兄弟。’

[P15] 25 虎先锋立即点起五十个精壮小妖，擂鼓摇旗，提两口赤铜刀，冲出洞来。见了悟空，厉声喝道：‘泼猴头，你来做甚！你师父是我拿了，你来却不是卖一个又饶一个？’
26 悟空闻言，心中大怒，举棒大喝一声：‘看棍！’那虎先锋持刀相迎。他两个各显神通，就在洞外厮杀起来。

[P16] 27 拼了一会，那虎怪招架不住，回头就走，他因在洞主面前夸了口，如今不敢回洞，便直往山坡上逃去。悟空怎肯放过，紧追不舍赶到那藏风山凹之间。只见八戒正在那里放马。
28 八戒忽然听到喊声，回头一看，是师兄追那虎怪。他就丢了马，举起钉钯，冷不防当头一筑。打得虎怪九个窟窿鲜血直冒，立即死去。

[P17] 29 八戒询问师父下落。悟空说：‘这妖怪把师父拿到洞中了。你打死这妖怪，算你的功劳。你仍旧在这里看着行李马匹，我去捉了那老妖，才能救得师父。’八戒连说：‘好，好！’
30 悟空一只手提着铁棒，一只手拖着死虎，来到黄风洞口，大声叫骂。

[P18] 31 洞里老妖听说虎怪惨死，已十分烦恼。又闻悟空在洞前骂战，便慌忙披挂，持一杆三股钢叉，率领大群小妖冲出洞来。
32 那老妖见悟空面容瘦削，身体矮小，不禁笑道：“我只道你是三头六臂的好汉，却原来是这般一个骷髅的病鬼！”

[P19] 33 悟空笑道：‘你外公虽是矮小，你若肯当头打一叉，就长六尺。’老妖呵呵大笑道：‘好！你站稳，吃我一叉！’说罢，劈头打来。
34 悟空不慌不忙，把腰躬一躬，足长了六尺，连本身有一丈长短。那老妖大吃一惊，手持钢叉猛力望悟空胸脯刺去。

[P20] 35 悟空提起金箍棒，使个乌龙掠地势，拨开钢叉，照老妖头上打去。二人在洞口，斗了三十回合，不分胜败。
36 悟空急切求胜，使个“身外身”的手段把毫毛揪下一把，向上一吹，叫声“变！”顿时有百来个悟空，各执铁棒，把那怪围在当中。

[P21] 37 那怪王害怕，也使出看家本领，把嘴一张，猛吹一口气，忽然黄风大作，飞沙走石。把百来个小悟空刮在半空，好像风车一般乱转。
38 悟空忙收毫毛，独自举棒来打，又被那怪劈脸喷了一口黄风。刮得悟空一双火眼金睛，难以睁开。老妖得胜回洞。

[P22] 39 悟空眼珠酸痛，泪水直流，只得跌跌撞撞来寻八戒。八戒见黄风大作，伏在山凹里，抱头缩颈，嘴里不住地念佛许愿，也正在着急哩。
40 悟空对八戒说：‘那老妖恶风厉害，一时难以取胜。’今日天色已晚，且寻个人家住下，等明天再救师父。他俩走出山口，只见路南山坡下，有一庄院，二人便去借宿。

[P23] 41 庄院里走出一位老者，见了他二人，并不骇异。问明了来意，便把他俩让进庄院。
42 悟空、八戒来到屋中，老者献茶办斋，十分殷勤。老者见悟空不住地淌泪揉眼，便问道：‘这位长老敢是害眼？’悟空把遭遇说了一遍。老者听罢，说有妙药可以医治。

[P24] 43 那老者取出一个玛瑙石的小瓶儿，拔开塞口，用玉簪挑了少许眼药给悟空点上。嘱咐他不要睁开，安心睡觉，明早就好。
44 八戒解了包袱，展开铺盖，请悟空睡下。悟空闭着眼睛乱摸，惹得八戒暗暗好笑。二人都挂念师父，直到三更方才睡着。

[P25] 45 五更时分，悟空抹抹脸，睁开眼睛道：‘果然好药，眼睛比往常更觉明亮了。’扭头一望，呀！但见四周高柳古槐，兄弟俩都睡在绿草地上，这里根本不是什么房舍。
46 八戒惊醒，见没了人家，慌得一骨碌爬将起来，叫道：‘我的马呢？’悟空道：‘树上拴的不是！’‘行李呢？’悟空道：‘在你身边哩！’

[P26] 47 八戒好生奇怪：“噫！我们也睡得忒死！怎么他家连夜拆房子搬家，一点也不曾听见动静？”悟空笑道：“呆子，不要胡说，你看那树上挂的是什么字帖儿？”
48 八戒走上前，揭下字帖，两人一看，不觉又惊又喜。原来是伽蓝菩萨暗中保护。庄院、老人，都是他变化的。

[P27] 49 两人望空拜了几拜，收拾动身。到了黄风洞附近，悟空道：‘兄弟，你在林子里守着，待老孙先去洞里打听打听，看如何下手。’
50 八戒道：‘你快去讨个师父死活的实信，假若师父死了，只好散伙；若是没死，我们好竭力尽心设法搭救。’悟空‘呸！’了一声说：‘莫乱谈，我去也。’说着身子一纵，早到黄风洞口。

[P28] 51 那把门的小妖，正在洞口打鼾。悟空不去惊动，念个咒语，摇身一变，变做一个花脚蚊虫。
52 悟空往小妖脸上叮了一口，那小妖翻身醒来，道：
“我的爷！好大蚊子，一口就叮了一个大疙瘩！”小妖抹抹嘴脸，见天色已亮，便把大门开了。

[P29] 53 悟空嘤嘤地飞将进去，只见那老妖一边收拾兵器，一边吩咐左右，道：‘只怕昨日那阵风不曾刮死猴头，说不定他今天还来，要小心防守。’
54 悟空直飞到后园，见师父被绑在定风桩上，愁眉苦脸，眼泪滚滚，嘴里不停地念着：‘悟空、悟能。’

[P30] 55 悟空落在唐僧的头上，叫了声：“师父”。唐僧听出是悟空的声音，喜道：“悟空，想死我了！你在哪里呀？”悟空道：“师父！你莫要心焦，我救你来了。
56 悟空又飞到前面，只见那老妖正在调兵遣将；又见一个小妖来报：“小的巡山，撞见一个长嘴大耳朵的和尚，那个毛脸和尚却寻不见。”

[P31] 57 老妖道：‘猴头不在，想必是被风吹死了，再不便是讨救兵去了。’众妖道：‘大王，他若去请些神兵来，那怎生是好？’
58 老妖笑道：‘神兵怕什么！要定得我的风势，只有灵吉菩萨才行。’悟空在屋梁上听得一清二楚，忙抽身飞出。

[P32] 59 悟空飞到林中，现出本相，把探得的情况欢欢喜喜地告诉了八戒。但又一想，却不知那灵吉菩萨在何处？正在为难，只见大路旁边走来一个老公公，细看时，正是太白金星。
60 悟空忙正正衣襟，上前施礼道：‘太白老头，动问一声，灵吉菩萨在哪里住？’太白金星道：‘灵吉在正南小须弥山，离此有三千里路。’

[P33] 61 悟空再问道：‘不知从哪条路去。’老人用手向南指道：‘走这条羊肠小路就是了。’悟空回头看路，那太白金星化作一道清风去了。
62 悟空搭救师父心切，嘱咐八戒在山林等候，自己跳在空中，驾筋斗云，往正南而去。不一会，见一座高山，山腰处祥云飘绕，果有一座禅院。

[P34] 63 悟空来到门前，见一道人，便上前施礼道：‘烦你传禀，唐僧徒弟孙悟空求见菩萨。’道人不敢怠慢，忙转身去报。
64 片刻，那灵吉菩萨整衣出迎，悟空登堂，言道：‘此来非为别事，我师父在黄风岭有难，要请菩萨降伏妖怪，救我师父。’

[P35] 65 灵吉菩萨道：‘当年我拿住那怪，饶了他性命，只望他弃邪归正，不想竟会加害令师。我有法宝收拾他，大圣只管放心。’
66 灵吉菩萨随即取了一颗‘定风丹’，一柄‘飞龙宝杖’，和悟空一齐驾云，来到黄风岭上。

[P36] 67 灵吉菩萨向下面端详一会，说道：‘大圣，那妖精有些怕我。你下去挑战，诱他出来，我好施法力。’
68 悟空依言，按落云头，举铁棒把洞门打破，叫道：
‘妖怪！快还我师父来！’

[P37] 69 小妖仓皇去报，那怪道：‘这泼猴如此无礼，活该作死！’说着，急忙披挂，手持钢叉，奔出洞来。
70 那怪一见悟空，不容分说，举叉当胸就刺。悟空侧身躲过，举棒迎战。战了几合，那怪掉头，又想张口呼风，吹走悟空。

[P38] 71 这时，灵吉菩萨从云端里将飞龙宝杖丢将下来。
72 那宝杖落到半空，突然变作一条八爪金龙，直扑下来。

[P39] 73 金龙伸开两爪，一把抓住妖精，提着头，两三摔，摔在山崖边。那怪现出原形，却是一个黄毛貂鼠。
74 悟空赶上，举棒要打，被灵吉菩萨拦住道：‘大圣，莫伤他性命，我还要带他去见如来，才好定罪哩。’悟空谢了灵吉菩萨，灵吉菩萨腾空而去。

[P40] 75 悟空赶到树林下，叫声：‘悟能兄弟，快牵马挑担来吧。’八戒正等得心焦，一听是师兄的声音，急急收拾，跑出树林。
76 八戒听说已拿住妖精，心中大喜。两人闯进洞里，解救师父。

[P41] 77 唐僧被松了绳索，问道：‘你二人怎生捉住妖精？如何赶来救我？’悟空便把伽蓝菩萨、太白金星暗中相助，以及灵吉菩萨降妖的事详细说了一遍。唐僧感激万分，连连望空祷告。
78 师徒三人在洞中，安排些茶饭吃了，方才离了黄风洞，直奔往西大路，取经去了。欲知后事如何，请看第十册《流沙河》。

[P1] Journey to the West Volume Six
Huangfeng Ridge

[P2] Huangfeng Ridge
Journey to the West, Part Nine
Original work: Wu Cheng'en
Adapted by: Pan Qinmeng
Illustrated by: Chi Zhenhua

Hebei Fine Arts Publishing House

Synopsis

On their journey to the West to obtain scriptures, Tang Sanzang and his disciples pass through Huangfeng Ridge. Tang Sanzang is captured by the Yellow Wind Demon. Sun Wukong goes to rescue his master but is also defeated by a single blast of the demon's strange wind. However, he does not become discouraged by his defeat. With the help of the Bodhisattva Lingji, he finally subdues the Yellow Wind Demon.

[P3] 1  Tang Sanzang, Wukong, and Bajie, the three disciples, were traveling west to fetch scriptures. As they walked, they saw a tall, steep mountain ahead. While looking at it, suddenly a whirlwind blew fiercely. Tang Sanzang exclaimed, 'Wukong, this wind is strange.'
2  Wukong said, 'Let me smell it.' He stepped aside from the wind, grabbed the tail of the gust, and smelled it, then shouted, 'Indeed, it smells fishy. This wind is not ordinary; it must be a demon causing trouble!'

[P4] 3 The words were not yet finished when a fierce roar was heard, and a spotted tiger leapt out from the hillside. The Tang Monk was terrified, his soul flying away, and he tumbled off his horse in a single somersault.
4 Pigsy put down his luggage, raised his rake, and roared: "You beast, where do you think you're going!" He rushed forward and swung his weapon down.

[P5] 5 The tiger stood up straight, raised its front left paw, grabbed its own chest, and with a 'hualala' sound, tore off its skin.
6 The monster revealed its evil form and shouted: 'Wait! I am the vanguard of King Huangfeng, sent to patrol the mountain to capture a few mortals for the king's wine. Where are you from, monk, to dare to wound me with weapons?'

[P6] 7 Pigsy explained his identity and then shouted, 'Get out of the way, and I'll spare your life. If you're defiant, my rake won't be merciful!' The demon, without hesitation, took a swift step and lunged at Pigsy. Pigsy swung his rake, but the demon, weaponless, turned and fled. Pigsy chased after him without letting up.
8 The demon fled to the foot of the hill, retrieved two copper blades from a pile of rocks, and turned to attack Pigsy. The two fought fiercely on the slope, striking back and forth, locked in a deadlock.

[P7] 9 Wukong supported Tang Sanzang and said, 'Master, don't be afraid. Sit still. I'll go help, knock that monster down, and then we can continue on our journey.' Tang Sanzang, still shaken, trembled with fear and kept reciting the 'Duo Xin Jing'.
10 Wukong saw that Bajie was full of spirit, fighting more bravely with each passing moment, and the monster was weakening, gradually retreating. He hurriedly called out, 'Brother, don't spare him!' The two of them swung their rake and staff, driving the monster down the mountain.

[P8] 11 The monster panicked, rolled on the ground, and revealed its true form — still a fierce tiger. Wukong and Bajie chased after it, determined to eliminate it completely.
12 The demon, seeing he was being pursued closely, used his escape technique, quickly peeled off his skin, covered a stone with it, and transformed his true body into a fierce wind, rushing straight to the roadside. He saw Master Tang sitting there, grabbed him in one motion, and carried him away on the wind.

[P9] 13 Wukong and Baijie still thought it was a real tiger that had fallen. Wukong raised his staff and struck with all his might, but it vibrated painfully in his hand; Baijie then swung his rake, and sparks flew. They realized they had hit a tiger skin covering a stone.
14 Wukong cried out in alarm: 'Oh no! We've fallen for his “Golden Cicada Sheds Its Shell” trick! Let's hurry back to check on Master, or we might be tricked by that monster.'

[P10] 15 Wukong and Bajie hurried back, seeing the white horse and luggage still there, but the Master was gone.
16 Wukong was furious and jumped like thunder, while Bajie was so anxious that tears streamed down his face. Wukong said: 
"Don't cry! Don't cry! Crying will dampen our spirit. The Master is surely on this mountain. Let's go find him quickly!"

[P11] 17 It is said that the monster brought Tang Sanzang to the cave entrance, held back the fierce wind, and hurriedly called a small demon guarding the door to report to King Huangfeng. King Huangfeng immediately gave orders for him to enter.
18 Tiger Vanguard held Tang Sanzang with both hands, knelt down, and said: 'Your Majesty, he is the monk Tang Sanzang from the Eastern Land, going to the Western Heaven to seek scriptures. I have captured him and present him to Your Majesty for your meal.'

[P12] 19 The Yellow Wind King, upon hearing this, was startled and said: 'I've heard that Master Sanzang has a disciple named Sun Wukong, who is immensely powerful and possesses great magical abilities. How were you able to capture him?'
20 The Tiger Vanguard recounted how he fought against Wukong and Bajie, and how he captured Tang Sanzang. Fearing that Tang Sanzang's disciples might be difficult to deal with, the Yellow Wind King ordered that Tang Sanzang be tied to the Wind-Resisting Stake in the back courtyard for three or five days, to observe the situation first.

[P13] 21 Then, Wukong and Bajie crossed mountains and ridges, searching everywhere for their master. Suddenly, they saw a cave府 emerging from beneath a cliff. Wukong told Bajie to find a sheltered mountain hollow, watch the luggage and horse, while he went to capture the demon.
22 Wukong rushed to the cave entrance and saw six large characters on the door: 'Huangfeng Ridge, Huangfeng Cave'. He raised his staff and shouted: 'Demon! Hand over my master at once, or I'll overturn your nest and flatten your dwelling!'

[P14] 23 The small demon guarding the door hurriedly reported the news. The Yellow Wind Demon, upon hearing that Wukong had come to his door, quickly summoned Tiger Vanguard and complained: 'I told you not to capture that Tang Monk! Now you've really brought his disciple here to cause trouble. What shall we do?'
24 Tiger Vanguard said: 'Your Majesty, please rest assured. Though I am not very capable, if I take fifty of my subordinates with me, I guarantee to bring back that Sun Wukong.' The Yellow Wind Demon replied: 'Very well. If you capture that monkey, I will be willing to become your sworn brother.'

[P15] 25 Tiger Vanguard immediately rallied fifty strong little demons, beat drums, waved flags, and brandished two copper blades as he charged out of the cave. Seeing Wukong, he shouted fiercely: 'You rascal monkey, what are you doing here! Your master is mine, so aren't you just trading one for another and letting one go?'
26 Upon hearing this, Wukong became furious and raised his staff, shouting: 'Take this!' The Tiger Vanguard met him with his blade. The two displayed their supernatural powers and began to fight fiercely outside the cave.

[P16] 27 After a while, the tiger demon couldn't hold his ground and turned to flee. Since he had boasted before the cave lord, he dared not return to the cave and fled straight up the hillside. Wukong, how could he let him go? He chased relentlessly and arrived at the hidden wind valley. He saw BaJie there, tending the horse.
28 BaJie suddenly heard a shout and turned around. It was his elder brother chasing the tiger demon. He dropped the horse, raised his rake, and struck the demon from behind. The blow opened nine holes in the tiger, blood gushing out, and the demon died immediately.

[P17] 29 Pigsy asked about Master's whereabouts. Wukong said: 'This demon has taken Master to the cave. If you kill this demon, it will count as your merit. You stay here and watch the luggage and horse, I will go capture the old demon to save Master.' Pigsy kept saying: 'Good, good!'
30 Wukong, holding the iron staff in one hand and dragging the dead tiger with the other, arrived at the entrance of Huangfeng Cave and shouted loudly.

[P18] 31 The old demon in the cave, having heard that the tiger demon was killed, was already very annoyed. Upon hearing that Wukong was taunting and challenging him at the cave entrance, he hurriedly put on his armor, took a three-pronged steel spear, and led a large group of small demons out of the cave.
32 The old demon, seeing Wukong's thin face and small body, couldn't help but laugh: "I thought you were a mighty hero with three heads and six arms, but you're actually just a bony, sickly ghost!"

[P19] 33 Wukong laughed, saying, 'Although your old man is short, if you dare to strike me with your spear from above, I'll grow six feet taller.' The old demon laughed heartily, 'Fine! Stand still, and take my spear!' Saying this, he swung his spear down.
34 Wukong remained calm, bent his waist slightly, and instantly grew six feet taller, making his entire body over ten feet long. The old demon was greatly shocked and fiercely thrust his steel spear toward Wukong's chest.

[P20] 35 Wukong raised his golden cudgel, used the 'Black Dragon Sweeping the Ground' maneuver, deflected the steel fork, and struck at the old demon's head. The two fought for thirty rounds at the cave entrance, neither gaining the upper hand.
36 Wukong, eager to win, used the 'Body Outside the Body' technique, plucked a handful of his hairs, blew them upward, and shouted, 'Transform!' Instantly, hundreds of Wukongs appeared, each wielding an iron rod, surrounding the demon.

[P21] 37 The demon king, frightened, also used his special skill, opened his mouth, and blew hard. Suddenly, a fierce yellow wind arose, causing sand and stones to fly. It swept the hundred or so small Sun Wukongs into the air, spinning them like a windmill.
38 Wukong quickly retracted his hair, fought alone with his staff, but was then sprayed in the face with a mouthful of yellow wind by the demon. The wind blew into Wukong's fiery golden eyes, making them hard to open. The old demon returned to his cave victorious.

[P22] 39 Wukong's eyes ached and tears streamed down as he stumbled and staggered to find BaJie. BaJie, seeing the fierce yellow wind, crouched in a hollow, hunched over, muttering prayers to the Buddha, also very anxious.
40 Wukong said to BaJie: 'That old demon's evil wind is too powerful; we can't defeat him right now.' It's already late, let's find a house to stay in and rescue Master tomorrow. They walked out of the mountain pass and saw a farmhouse at the foot of the southern slope; the two went to ask for lodging.

[P23] 41 An old man came out of the courtyard, saw the two of them, and was not surprised. After learning their purpose, he invited them into the courtyard.
42 Wukong and Bajie entered the house, and the old man served them tea and a meal, being very hospitable. Seeing Wukong constantly wiping his eyes and crying, the old man asked, 'Master, are you suffering from eye trouble?' Wukong told him about his ordeal. After listening, the old man said he had a miraculous remedy that could cure it.

[P24] 43 The old man took out a small bottle made of agate, opened the stopper, and used a jade hairpin to apply a little eye medicine to Wukong. He told him not to open his eyes, to sleep soundly, and it would be fine by morning.
44 Bajie unpacked his bag, spread out the bedding, and asked Wukong to lie down. Wukong, with his eyes closed, fumbled around, which made Bajie secretly laugh. Both of them were worried about their master and didn't fall asleep until the third watch.

[P25] 45 At the fifth watch, Wukong rubbed his face and opened his eyes, saying, 'Indeed, the medicine is good; my eyes feel brighter than usual.' He turned his head and gasped, 'Look! All around are tall willows and ancient locust trees; the two of us are sleeping on the green grass. This is certainly not a house.
46 Bajie woke up in alarm, seeing that the house was gone. He scrambled up in a panic and cried, 'Where is my horse?' Wukong replied, 'Isn't it tied to the tree?' 'What about the luggage?' Wukong answered, 'It's right beside you!'

[P26] 47 Pigsy was very puzzled: “Huh! We slept so soundly! How could they have torn down the house and moved out overnight without us hearing a thing?” Wukong laughed: “Fool, don’t talk nonsense. Look at what’s hanging on that tree — what kind of notice is it?”
48 Pigsy walked forward, took down the notice, and upon seeing it, both were amazed and delighted. It turned out that the Guardian Deity had secretly protected them. The courtyard and the old man were all his transformations.

[P27] 49 The two bowed to the sky several times, then packed up and set off. Upon reaching near the Yellow Wind Cave, Wukong said: 'Brother, you stay hidden in the woods. I'll go into the cave first to scout around and see how to proceed.'
50 Bajie said: 'You'd better go and find out for sure whether our master is alive or dead. If he's dead, we might as well break up; if he's still alive, we can do our best to rescue him.' Wukong spat and said: 'Don't talk nonsense, I'm going!' Saying that, he leaped into the air and arrived at the entrance of the Yellow Wind Cave.

[P28] 51 The little demon guarding the door was snoring at the cave entrance. Wukong didn't disturb him, recited a spell, and transformed into a spotted mosquito.
52 Wukong bit the little demon on the face. The demon woke up, turned over, and said: 
"My goodness! What a big mosquito, one bite and it left a huge bump!" The demon rubbed his face, saw that it was already daylight, and opened the door.

[P29] 53 Wukong flew in quietly. He saw the old demon putting away his weapons and giving orders to his subordinates: 'I'm afraid yesterday's wind didn't kill that monkey. He might come back today. Be careful and guard well.'
54 Wukong flew straight to the back garden and saw his master tied to the Wind-Still Stake, looking worried and sorrowful, tears streaming down his face, constantly muttering: 'Wukong, Wuneng.'

[P30] 55 Wukong landed on Tang Sanzang's head and called out, "Master!" Tang Sanzang recognized Wukong's voice and joyfully said, "Wukong, I've missed you so much! Where are you?" Wukong replied, "Master! Don't worry, I've come to save you.
56 Wukong flew forward again and saw the old demon commanding his troops; then a small demon reported, "Your Highness, while patrolling the mountain, I saw a monk with a long mouth and big ears, but the hairy-faced monk could not be found."

[P31] 57 The old demon said, 'The monkey is not here. He must have been blown to death by the wind, or else he has gone to fetch reinforcements.' The other demons said, 'Your Majesty, what if he goes to summon heavenly soldiers? What then?' 
58 The old demon laughed, 'What do I fear heavenly soldiers for! To counter my wind power, only the Bodhisattva Lingji can do it.' Wukong, listening clearly from the beam, hurriedly flew out.

[P32] 59 Wukong flew to the forest, revealed his true form, and happily told Bajie what he had discovered. But then he thought, 'I still don't know where the Lingji Bodhisattva is!' Just as he was troubled, he saw an old man walking by the roadside. Upon closer look, it was the Star of White Jade.
60 Wukong quickly straightened his clothes and bowed, saying: 'Old Master Taibai, I must ask—where does the Lingji Bodhisattva reside?' The Star of White Jade replied: 'Lingji is at the Small Xumi Mountain to the south, three thousand li away.'

[P33] 61 Wukong asked again, 'I don't know which path to take.' The old man pointed south and said, 'Take this narrow winding path.' Wukong looked back at the path, and the Taibai JinXing had turned into a gentle breeze and disappeared.
62 Wukong, eager to rescue his master, instructed Bajie to wait in the forest, then jumped into the air, riding his cloud, heading south. Soon, he saw a tall mountain with auspicious clouds swirling around its waist, and indeed, there was a monastery.

[P34] 63 Wukong arrived at the gate and saw a Taoist. He stepped forward and bowed, saying, 'Please convey my message: Tang Seng's disciple Sun Wukong seeks to see the Bodhisattva.' The Taoist, not daring to be negligent, hurried off to report.
64 In a moment, Bodhisattva Lingji came out to greet him. Wukong entered the hall and said, 'I have come for no other reason. My master is in trouble at Huangfeng Ridge. I beg the Bodhisattva to subdue the demon and save my master.'

[P35] 65 Lingji Bodhisattva said: 'Years ago, I captured that demon, spared his life, and hoped he would abandon evil and return to the righteous path. I never expected he would harm your master. I have a magical treasure to deal with him. Great Sage, please rest assured.'
66 Lingji Bodhisattva then took a 'Wind-Stilling Pill' and a 'Flying Dragon Staff', and flew with Wukong to Huangfeng Ridge.

[P36] 67 Lingji Bodhisattva looked down for a moment and said, 'Great Sage, that demon is somewhat afraid of me. Go down and challenge him, lure him out, so I can use my magical power.'
68 Wukong followed his instructions, landed from the clouds, raised his iron staff to break the cave door, and shouted:
'Demon! Return my master to me!'

[P37] 69 The little demon hurried to report. The monster said, 'This rascal monkey is so rude, he deserves to die!' Saying that, he quickly put on his armor, grabbed his steel fork, and rushed out of the cave.
70 The monster, upon seeing Wukong, didn't hesitate and thrust his fork straight at Wukong's chest. Wukong dodged to the side and raised his staff to fight back. After a few rounds, the monster turned away and tried to open his mouth to blow wind, intending to blow Wukong away.

[P38] 71 At this moment, the Bodhisattva Lingji threw the Flying Dragon Staff down from the clouds.
72 The staff, as it fell halfway through the air, suddenly transformed into an eight-clawed golden dragon, diving straight down.

[P39] 73 The golden dragon opened its two claws, grabbed the demon, lifted it by the head, and threw it two or three times, finally tossing it to the edge of the cliff. The demon revealed its true form — a yellow-furred weasel.
74 Wukong rushed forward, raised his staff to strike, but was stopped by Lingji Bodhisattva, who said: 'Great Sage, do not harm his life; I still need to take him to see the Buddha, so that his guilt can be properly judged.' Wukong thanked Lingji Bodhisattva, and Lingji Bodhisattva soared into the sky.

[P40] 75 Wukong arrived at the grove and called out, 'Wuneng brother, quickly bring the horse and carry the load!' Bajie, who had been waiting anxiously, heard his elder brother's voice and hurriedly gathered his things, running out of the grove.
76 Bajie, hearing that the demon had been captured, was overjoyed. The two rushed into the cave to rescue their master.

[P41] 77 The Tang Monk, having his ropes untied, asked: 'How did you two capture the demon? How did you come to rescue me?' Wukong then told him in detail about how the伽蓝菩萨, the White-Robed Immortal, and the Lingji Bodhisattva had helped subdue the demon. The Tang Monk was deeply grateful and kept praying towards the sky.
78 The master and his two disciples ate some tea and food in the cave, then left the Yellow Wind Cave and headed straight west on the great road to continue their journey for the scriptures. To learn what happens next, please read Volume Ten, 'The River of Flowing Sand'.

[P42] Catalog of "Journey to the West" Illustrated Stories

full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为《西游记之六》的封面或标题页，画面描绘了孙悟空与黄风怪在山岭间对战的场景，下方标题为“黄风岭”。
[P2] 本页为《西游记》之九《黄风岭》的版权页和内容提要，介绍了唐僧师徒在黄风岭遭遇黄风怪，孙悟空在灵吉菩萨帮助下最终降伏妖怪的故事情节。
[P3] 唐僧师徒三人行至黄风岭，突遇一阵怪风，唐僧感到奇怪，孙悟空闻风后判断是妖怪作祟。
[P4] 唐僧师徒在黄风岭遭遇一只斑斓猛虎，唐僧受惊从马上跌下，猪八戒则举起钉耙上前迎战。
[P5] 本页描绘了黄风岭的老虎现出原形并剥下虎皮，随后自称黄风大王部下先锋的妖怪现身，质问孙悟空为何用兵器伤它。
[P6] 猪八戒与黄风岭的妖怪交战，妖怪先徒手攻击，被八戒追击后逃至山坡下取出铜刀，双方随即展开激烈搏斗，难分胜负。
[P7] 孙悟空安慰受惊的唐僧，表示自己去助阵；随后与猪八戒合力将妖怪逼下山。
[P8] 本页描绘了黄风岭妖怪在被孙悟空和猪八戒追赶时，现出原形为猛虎，随后又使用脱身法化作狂风，掳走唐僧的情节。
[P9] 孙悟空和猪八戒误以为打倒了真老虎，结果发现只是一张虎皮盖着石头，悟空意识到中了妖怪的“金蝉脱壳”之计，急忙催促八戒回去查看师父的安危。
[P10] 孙悟空和猪八戒返回原地，发现白马和行李仍在，但师父唐僧不见了。孙悟空怒不可遏，劝猪八戒不要哭泣，并决定立即在山上寻找师父。
[P11] 妖怪将唐僧擒至洞口，命小妖禀报黄风大王；虎先锋将唐僧献给黄风大王，称其为东土大唐法师，欲供大王食用。
[P12] 黄风大王得知捉住唐僧后，对虎先锋如何擒获唐僧表示惊讶，并因惧怕孙悟空而下令将唐僧暂时绑在后院的定风桩上，观察动静。
[P13] 孙悟空和猪八戒在寻找唐僧时发现一座山崖下的洞府，悟空让八戒看守行李，自己前去捉拿妖怪。悟空抵达洞口，看到门上写着“黄风岭黄风洞”，便高声叫骂，威胁妖怪交出师父。
[P14] 黄风怪得知孙悟空寻上门来，责怪虎先锋捉了唐僧引来麻烦；虎先锋立下军令状，承诺带五十小妖捉拿孙悟空，黄风怪答应若成功便与他结为兄弟。
[P15] 虎先锋率众小妖出洞迎战孙悟空，双方在洞外展开激战。
[P16] 孙悟空追击虎先锋至山坡，猪八戒闻声赶来，趁其不备用钉耙击毙虎先锋。
[P17] 孙悟空让猪八戒看守行李马匹，自己带着打死的虎先锋前往黄风洞口叫骂，准备捉拿妖怪救师父。
[P18] 黄风怪得知虎先锋被杀后大怒，披挂上阵，率领小妖冲出洞府迎战孙悟空。他见到孙悟空身形瘦小，便嘲笑其不像传说中的勇猛好汉。
[P19] 孙悟空与黄风怪对峙，悟空以言语挑衅，黄风怪挥叉攻击；悟空随即施展法术变高，黄风怪惊愕之余猛刺悟空胸脯。
[P20] 孙悟空与黄风怪在洞口激战三十回合不分胜负，随后悟空使用“身外身”法术，变出百个分身围攻妖怪。
[P21] 黄风怪施展黄风神通，将孙悟空变出的百个分身吹得四处乱转；孙悟空收起分身独自迎战，又被黄风刮伤火眼金睛，最终黄风怪得胜回洞。
[P22] 孙悟空因被黄风怪的黄风刮伤眼睛，疼痛难忍，跌跌撞撞去找猪八戒。两人商议暂且放弃战斗，天黑后去山下村庄借宿，明日再救师父。
[P23] 孙悟空和猪八戒来到一户人家借宿，一位老者热情接待了他们。老者见孙悟空眼睛受伤，询问后得知其遭遇，并表示有药可以医治。
[P24] 老者为孙悟空点上眼药并嘱咐他安心睡觉，猪八戒为孙悟空铺好床铺，两人因挂念师父而辗转难眠，直至深夜才睡着。
[P25] 孙悟空眼睛痊愈后发现与猪八戒睡在野外，猪八戒惊醒后发现马和行李仍在身边。
[P26] 孙悟空和猪八戒发现昨夜借宿的村庄一夜之间消失，树上留有字帖，揭下后得知是伽蓝菩萨化作庄院和老人暗中保护了他们。
[P27] 孙悟空和猪八戒在黄风洞附近商议对策，悟空决定独自潜入洞中探听师父下落，猪八戒则在林中守候，随后悟空驾云直奔黄风洞口。
[P28] 孙悟空化作花脚蚊虫潜入黄风洞，咬醒守门小妖，小妖以为是大蚊子叮咬，便在天亮后打开了洞门。
[P29] 孙悟空化作蚊虫潜入黄风洞，发现老妖正在吩咐小妖小心防守；随后他飞到后园，看到师父被绑在定风桩上，正焦急地呼唤他和猪八戒的名字。
[P30] 孙悟空化作蚊虫潜入黄风洞，落在唐僧头上与之相认，唐僧激动呼唤，孙悟空安慰师父。随后孙悟空飞至洞前，发现老妖正在调兵遣将，一个小妖报告说在山中撞见了长嘴大耳朵的和尚（猪八戒），但没找到毛脸和尚（孙悟空）。
[P31] 黄风洞内，老妖认为孙悟空已死或去求救兵，众妖担忧；老妖自信能抵御神兵，唯灵吉菩萨可破其风势，孙悟空在屋梁上听清后立即飞出。
[P32] 孙悟空向猪八戒报告探听情况后，因不知灵吉菩萨所在而发愁，恰逢太白金星路过，便上前询问，得知灵吉菩萨在正南小须弥山，距离三千里。
[P33] 孙悟空向太白金星问明前往小须弥山的路径后，立即驾云南行，途中见到一座祥云缭绕的高山，山腰处有一座禅院。
[P34] 孙悟空到达小须弥山，向道人求见灵吉菩萨，随后进入禅院，向灵吉菩萨说明唐僧在黄风岭遇险，请求其降伏妖怪救师父。
[P35] 灵吉菩萨向孙悟空保证能降伏妖怪，并取出定风丹和飞龙宝杖，与孙悟空一同驾云前往黄风岭。
[P36] 灵吉菩萨与孙悟空一同前往黄风岭，菩萨建议孙悟空下凡挑战妖怪以引其现身，孙悟空依言打破洞门，高声呼喊妖怪归还师父。
[P37] 黄风怪得知孙悟空打破洞门后，怒斥其无礼并披挂出洞迎战。孙悟空与黄风怪交手数回合，黄风怪欲张口呼风将孙悟空吹走。
[P38] 灵吉菩萨从云端抛下飞龙宝杖，宝杖在半空中化作一条八爪金龙，直扑向黄风怪。
[P39] 金龙将黄风怪擒获并摔在山崖边，妖怪现出黄毛貂鼠原形。孙悟空欲举棒击打，被灵吉菩萨劝阻，菩萨称要带妖怪去见如来定罪，随后腾空离去。
[P40] 孙悟空赶到树林，叫八戒牵马挑担；八戒得知妖怪已被擒，与孙悟空一同闯入洞中解救师父。
[P41] 唐僧被救后询问孙悟空如何降伏妖怪，孙悟空讲述了伽蓝菩萨、太白金星和灵吉菩萨相助的经过，唐僧感激不已。随后师徒三人用过茶饭，离开黄风洞，继续西行取经。
